meaning: A set of ways one program can ask another program for information or an action.
comparison: Like a restaurant menu: it tells you what you can ask for and how to order it.

meaning: A private code used to identify an app when it calls a service. It can let someone use your account or allowance.
comparison: Like a keycard charged to your room: keep it private and replace it if it leaks.

meaning: Extra information given to a command or function to tell it what to do.
comparison: Like adding “no ice” to a drink order. In --port 8768, 8768 is the value for the port option.

meaning: Checking who someone is, often through a password or sign-in service.
comparison: Like showing your ID at the entrance.

meaning: Checking what an identified person is allowed to see or do.
comparison: Like your ticket deciding which rooms you may enter after your ID is checked.

meaning: The part of an app that handles work such as checking access and saving records, usually away from the screen you see.
comparison: Like a restaurant kitchen: the dining area sends orders to it.

meaning: A separate saved copy you can use if something goes wrong.
comparison: Like keeping a spare copy of an important document somewhere safe.

meaning: A separate line of changes in a code project, so work can happen before it is combined with the main version.
comparison: Like drafting an alternate chapter without changing the published book.

meaning: The app you use to open websites.
comparison: Like a window into a website. Chrome and Edge are browsers; YARN is the app shown inside one.

meaning: A mistake that makes software behave differently from what was intended.
comparison: Like a vending machine giving the wrong drink after you press the right button.

meaning: Preparing source code and other files into a form ready to run or publish.
comparison: Like turning ingredients and a recipe into a packed meal.

meaning: A saved shortcut copy of data used to make later requests faster. It can sometimes be out of date.
comparison: Like keeping a frequently used page on your desk instead of fetching the whole book again.

meaning: A way to use a program by typing commands instead of clicking buttons.
comparison: Like giving a written instruction to a helper. The terminal is the window; a CLI is the program you talk to in it.

meaning: The program or device asking another program for something. A browser is often a client.
comparison: Like a customer placing an order with a shop.

meaning: Make a local copy of a Git repository, including its version history.
comparison: Like copying a project notebook along with its earlier revisions.

meaning: Written instructions that tell a computer what to do.
comparison: Like a recipe, but written in a language a computer can follow.

meaning: The coding AI you work with to inspect, write, and change code.
comparison: Like a coding helper: you still need to check that the result does what you wanted.

meaning: An instruction you type for your computer to carry out.
comparison: Like a written task: python server.py tells Python to run the file server.py.

meaning: A recorded set of changes in Git, usually with a short note explaining it.
comparison: Like a named checkpoint you can compare with earlier checkpoints. It does not automatically publish the app.

meaning: Settings that tell a program how to behave in a particular setup.
comparison: Like choosing the temperature and cycle on a washing machine.

aliases: console window command prompt cmd powershell terminal devtools
meaning: A text area where you can see program messages and sometimes type instructions. A console window often means Command Prompt, PowerShell, or a terminal. A browser console is a different place inside browser developer tools.
comparison: Like a conversation window with your computer. If told to “keep the console open,” leave that command window running.

meaning: Browser rules controlled by server responses that decide whether a page can read responses from a different origin.
comparison: Like permission to receive a reply from another building. It does not replace checking who may access the data.

meaning: Information used to prove identity or gain access, such as a password, API key, or login token.
comparison: Like keys and ID cards: avoid putting them in a public file or screenshot.

meaning: Code that controls a web page’s appearance, such as colors, spacing, and layout.
comparison: Like the clothes and interior design of a page.

meaning: An organized place where an app stores and finds information.
comparison: Like a filing cabinet with a system for finding and updating each record.

meaning: Investigate why something is wrong and work out how to fix it.
comparison: Like tracing which step in a recipe made the cake sink.

meaning: Code from another project that your app relies on.
comparison: Like a ready-made ingredient: useful, but its quality and version matter too.

meaning: Put a version of an app into the environment where people will use it.
comparison: Like opening a finished shop to visitors. Saving code alone does not deploy it.

meaning: A folder that holds files or other folders.
comparison: Like a drawer in a filing cabinet. “Open the project directory” means open its folder.

meaning: A readable name used to find a website or service, such as example.com.
comparison: Like a shop’s street address written in words instead of the map coordinates.

meaning: A particular address and request method that an app responds to.
comparison: Like a specific service counter: one handles sign-in, another handles messages.

meaning: The surroundings in which software runs: its machine, settings, and installed tools.
comparison: Like a kitchen: the same recipe may work differently if the equipment or ingredients change.

meaning: A named setting supplied to a running program. Some hold secrets. A .env file is one common way to load them.
comparison: Like a labeled note handed to the cook. A note containing a password must stay private.

meaning: A message or condition saying a task could not finish as expected.
comparison: Like a warning light: copy the exact message so the cause can be investigated.

meaning: A number a program returns when it finishes. Zero usually means success; other numbers need the program’s explanation.
comparison: Like a delivery receipt: it tells you how the task ended.

meaning: Prepared example files or data used for repeatable tests or demonstrations.
comparison: Like a practice patient in a training exercise. YARN’s judge fixtures are fictional, not your real app’s data.

meaning: A set of tools and rules that provides a starting structure for an app.
comparison: Like a house frame: you build your rooms inside its structure.

meaning: The visible, interactive part of an app: pages, buttons, forms, and screens.
comparison: Like a restaurant’s dining area, where customers interact with the service.

meaning: A named piece of code that performs a task when called.
comparison: Like a reusable recipe step named “make sauce.”

meaning: A tool that records code changes so you can compare versions and work on separate branches.
comparison: Like a detailed project history with checkpoints.

meaning: A service where people can store Git projects online and collaborate.
comparison: Like an online shared shelf for project histories. Git is the tracking tool; GitHub is one place to host them.

meaning: The code describing a web page’s content and structure.
comparison: Like the page’s skeleton: headings, paragraphs, forms, and buttons.

meaning: The rules browsers and servers use to exchange web requests and replies. HTTPS protects the connection with encryption.
comparison: Like a delivery system; HTTPS uses a sealed, protected route. It does not guarantee the website itself is trustworthy.

meaning: Put a program or package on a computer so it can be used.
comparison: Like adding a tool to your toolbox. Downloading a ZIP does not always install its contents.

meaning: A text format for storing structured information using named fields, lists, and values.
comparison: Like a neatly labeled form that programs can read. Its punctuation must follow strict rules.

meaning: Reusable code that other code can call. In another context, “Library” may mean your saved files.
comparison: Like a shelf of ready-made tools, rather than building each tool yourself.

meaning: Running or stored on the computer you are using, rather than on a remote computer.
comparison: Like keeping a document on your own desk. A local app may still contact outside services if enabled.

meaning: An address pointing back to the same computer that opens it.
comparison: Like saying “this house.” A localhost link on your laptop does not open your laptop’s app on someone else’s phone.

meaning: A file recording the dependency versions resolved by a package manager.
comparison: Like an exact shopping receipt, helping another setup use the same ingredients.

meaning: A record of messages about what a program has done or what went wrong.
comparison: Like a ship’s logbook. Logs can contain private information, so review them before sharing.

meaning: Combine changes from one code branch into another.
comparison: Like combining edits from two drafts. Conflicting edits may need a person to decide what to keep.

meaning: A planned change to a database’s structure or stored data.
comparison: Like reorganizing a filing cabinet while making sure the old records still fit.

meaning: A controlled stand-in for a real component during a test.
comparison: Like a practice phone call with a colleague pretending to be a customer. Passing it does not prove the real service works.

meaning: A program that lets JavaScript run outside a web page, such as on a local computer or server.
comparison: Like a different stage where JavaScript can perform without a browser.

meaning: A tool commonly used to download and manage JavaScript packages and run project scripts.
comparison: Like a supply clerk for project ingredients. Some install commands can also run scripts.

meaning: Working without an internet connection for that task.
comparison: Like using a paper notebook. YARN’s judge checks work offline; opening an outside link still uses the internet.

meaning: A bundle of reusable code or tools that can be installed together.
comparison: Like a boxed kit containing parts and instructions.

meaning: A set of proposed or applied changes to files.
comparison: Like tracked edits in a document. A patch still needs review and checking.

meaning: The address of a file or folder on a computer. An absolute path starts from the drive or root; a relative path starts from your current folder.
comparison: Like a full street address versus “the room next door.”

meaning: A rule deciding whether a person or program may do something, such as read a file or delete a message.
comparison: Like a door pass that may allow entry but not rearranging the room.

meaning: A numbered doorway used to reach a particular program on a computer.
comparison: Like an apartment number after the building address. In 127.0.0.1:8768, 8768 is the port. “Already in use” means another program is using it.

meaning: The real app environment used by actual users.
comparison: Like the restaurant during service. Changes here can affect real people and data.

meaning: A proposal to bring changes from one branch into another, often with a review first.
comparison: Like asking someone to approve a revised chapter before it becomes part of the main book.

meaning: Send local Git commits to a remote Git repository.
comparison: Like sending your saved draft to the shared shelf. This only publishes the app if a deployment process is set up to run afterward.

meaning: A programming language and the program that runs code written in that language.
comparison: Like a language plus its reader. In py -3 server.py, the Windows Python launcher runs the Python file.

meaning: Ask the browser to load the page again. A hard refresh also tries to bypass cached page files.
comparison: Like asking for a fresh copy of a handout. It does not restart the server.

meaning: A project’s files and, when tracked by Git, their change history.
comparison: Like the whole project binder, not just one page of code.

meaning: A message asking a program for data or an action. The answer is the response.
comparison: Like sending an order and getting a reply saying what happened.

meaning: Stop a program, then start it again so it starts fresh. Some changes require this.
comparison: Like closing and reopening a shop after changing its setup. Refreshing a browser page alone does not restart its server.

meaning: Return to an earlier version after a problem. Database or external changes may need separate recovery.
comparison: Like replacing a revised draft with an earlier copy; it does not automatically undo everything that happened afterward.

meaning: The main folder from which a project’s files are organized.
comparison: Like the binder holding all the project’s sections. “Run from the project root” means open the command window in that folder.

meaning: Start following a program’s instructions.
comparison: Like pressing play on a recording. Opening a script in Notepad only displays its text; it does not run it.

meaning: The software and conditions that let code run. “At runtime” means while the program is actually operating.
comparison: Like the equipment and stage during a performance, rather than the written script.

meaning: A structured file format that security tools can use to share findings.
comparison: Like a common report form different inspectors can fill in. Importing it does not independently prove its claims.

meaning: Use a tool to examine specified files or behavior for particular signs of problems.
comparison: Like an inspection with a checklist: items outside the checklist can still be unknown.

meaning: A file of instructions run by another program or command shell.
comparison: Like a to-do list for the computer. Its file ending helps identify which program should run it.

meaning: A sensitive value that must stay private, such as a password, access token, or signing key.
comparison: Like a safe combination. Replacing it after a leak is called rotation.

meaning: A running program that receives requests and sends replies. It can run on your computer or another machine.
comparison: Like a service desk. Closing YARN’s command window stops that local desk from answering.

meaning: A way an app remembers a user’s visit or signed-in state across requests.
comparison: Like a temporary visitor pass after sign-in. It should expire or be revocable.

meaning: The human-readable instructions and supporting files used to build or run an app.
comparison: Like the original recipe and preparation notes, rather than just the finished meal.

meaning: A separate environment used to try changes before they reach production.
comparison: Like a dress rehearsal. Keep real secrets and personal data out unless that use is deliberately approved.

meaning: Files sent to the browser largely as stored, such as images, stylesheets, and JavaScript files.
comparison: Like ready-printed handouts; the JavaScript inside can still make the page interactive.

aliases: shell command window powershell cmd console
meaning: A window for interacting with text-based programs. A shell, such as PowerShell, reads the commands you type there.
comparison: Like a front desk and interpreter together: the window shows the conversation, and the shell understands your instructions.

aliases: unit test integration test smoke test
meaning: A repeatable check comparing what software does with what you expect. A smoke test is a quick check of the main flow.
comparison: Like trying the lights before opening a shop. Passing a few checks does not prove every possible action works.

aliases: access token auth token AI token
meaning: In sign-in, a value used to show access rights. In AI usage, a token is a small chunk of text used for processing and usage measurement.
comparison: Like a visitor pass in security, or counted pieces of text in AI. The meaning depends on the sentence.

meaning: The full address of a web resource, possibly including a protocol, host, port, and path.
comparison: Like a full delivery address. http://127.0.0.1:8768/ points to the local demo’s doorway.

meaning: Checking whether something meets specific rules or expectations.
comparison: Like checking a form’s fields before accepting it. Valid format does not prove every claim inside is true.

meaning: A named place in a program used to refer to a value.
comparison: Like a labeled box whose contents the program can read or change.

meaning: A particular edition of a program or package.
comparison: Like different editions of a textbook. Instructions for one edition may not work for another.

meaning: An isolated place for a Python project’s installed packages.
comparison: Like a separate toolbox for each project, helping their tools avoid clashing.

meaning: A weakness that could let someone cause harm or gain access they should not have.
comparison: Like a lock that can be bypassed. A warning or risky setting still needs evidence to establish the actual problem.

meaning: An automatic request one service sends to another when a particular event happens.
comparison: Like a doorbell announcing a delivery instead of you repeatedly checking the doorstep.

meaning: A file that packs other files and folders together, often making them smaller. Extracting unpacks them.
comparison: Like a suitcase: unpack the whole project before running it. Zipping is not the same as encrypting or hiding secrets.
